chiplets_assessment: A modular chiplet architecture is the right technical solution for D2 because the measured C6 leaf bottleneck (k >= 22 for dispatch alone, k = 21..23 per rule) comes from repeating full-carrier range checks, frame/task multiplexers, PROG walks, and full-carrier Poseidon hashes rather than rule-specific transition logic. On midnight-proofs 0.8.3 (Halo2/KZG) and midnight-circuits 7.3.0, all chiplets (PROG ROM, memory/stacks, 128-bit arithmetic/range, and Poseidon) must reside as modular regions inside a single circuit connected by Halo2's native single-phase ConstraintSystem::lookup_any bus, because the in-circuit VerifierGadget asserts a single challenge phase (ruling out a multi-phase LogUp bus without a gadget fork) and cross-proof buses would multiply 250k-row non-native MSM verifiers. Crucially, this chiplet processor belongs in a separate multi-step segment leaf U (feeding run-lift R under core keys {U, R, F, N, C, D}) rather than inline inside the binary node N: every chiplet advice column and lookup product added to N enlarges N's own verifying key and adds 2x variable bases to N's self-verifier MSM (already 730,243 rows) and 1x to D (already 929,166 rows), whereas isolating the chiplets in U gives the VM 100% of a k=19..20 domain for T=64..256 steps per proof and keeps N, C, and D small and chiplet-agnostic.
proposed_requirement_text: SRC-021 (genesis): When h_pre == 0, the segment leaf U SHALL prove in circuit that its pre-state commitment equals Init(prog_d, input_d), binding Eval(entry) opened from prog_root in prog_d, initial and remaining fuel, stack_limit, and the initial input commitment opened from input_d, Pending/Running outcome, zeroed helper/result registers and counters, empty frame and helper-task hash chains, canonical initial roots for all four append tables (data, data_fields, env, value_slots), and empty deps_d; the seal rule SHALL require h_lo == 0, and equality with a caller-supplied init_d or off-chain recomputation SHALL NOT be acceptance authority.

GP-001 / SRC-013 / SRC-014 (chiplet leaf U): The universal leaf U SHALL be one fixed relation keyed over a fixed processor register file and rule transition table that proves a segment of up to T consecutive microsteps (1 <= steps <= T, disabled tail rows constrained to identity with zero step contribution) at k_U <= 20 by routing program reads, memory/stack operations, 128-bit arithmetic/range checks, and Poseidon hashes over a single-phase lookup_any bus to in-circuit chiplet regions, authenticating all cross-segment state against pre_d and post_d commitments.

GPR-MEMORY (chiplet bus and memory integrity): Each active lookup_any bus request in U SHALL be uniquely keyed by its (step_index, slot_id) and bound to a verified chiplet row; writes to the four append-only tables (data, data_fields, env, value_slots) SHALL enforce monotonic allocation-counter indexing and read-after-write consistency, and frames and helper tasks SHALL be authenticated as Poseidon hash chains with top entries in registers.

GP-004 arity — OWNER AMENDMENT: Replace the first bullet of GP-4 in general-purpose.md with: 'A node N at k=20 takes at least two proofs (arity >= 2), each either a prior node proof (N) or new work proved under a core lift key (R or F), so any combination of prior proofs and new work is reached by nesting under the same fixed key set {U, R, F, N, C, D}; every node shape is served by the same key set with no per-depth or per-level key.'

GP-003 scope — OWNER AMENDMENT: Add to GP-3 in general-purpose.md: 'Circuits on the same curve, commitment scheme, and SRS whose constraint system is a Midnight stdlib configuration (an (arch, k, public_inputs_len, transcript) class with two instance columns and one challenge phase) are verified through one class adapter key admitted to the registry as data without changing any core key or contract; circuits outside that configuration are verified either when an adapter for their configuration is admitted as registry data or by executing an authenticated verifier program across segments of U.'

GPR-ADAPTER-LEDGER (GP-3 Compact proofs): Where a foreign claim asserts verification of a Compact proof for GP-3 acceptance, the adapter A_c SHALL verify the supplied ledger-format proof[v5] bytes under the registered verifier-key[v7] without the circuit witness, enforcing the keyed 64-byte Blake2b ledger transcript (with domain separator and common/challenge prefixes), exact public-input length, complete byte consumption, and curve/subgroup checks, and SHALL tag the claim kind as `ledger`; Poseidon re-proofs under the same key SHALL be tagged `reproved` and SHALL serve only as intermediate integration tests.

GPR-STORAGE-DEPTH (GP-1 capacity): Committed memory trees in U SHALL support witnessed path depths up to the 64-bit machine address/height bound (or, if the owner adopts an OWNER AMENDMENT to GP-1, a fixed depth of 32 for the program and data tables alongside unbounded hash chains for frames and helper tasks) under a single fixed key set.

GPR-NODE-CLOSING (named lifts and two-stage closing): The node N SHALL verify up to two proofs under {N, R, F} using one-hot key and fixed-base name selection, normalizing disabled slots to the canonical neutral accumulator encoding by lane selection without per-slot in-circuit MSM collapse; the closing proof C SHALL verify the root N proof, fold N's own and carried accumulators, and resolve the fixed bases of N, R, and F, and the decider D SHALL verify C, pin C's key, fold C's own and carried accumulators, resolve C's fixed bases, and check the final KZG pairing.
